asks: which lane should I gank
who do I gank
where should I go gank
which lane is gankable right now
top or bot gank
say: Gank the lane where the wave sits on your side and your laner has crowd control, or keep farming if no lane looks like that.
more: A wave on your side means the enemy has a long walk home, so even a slow gank gets time on him.
Crowd control from your laner matters more than your own damage; it decides whether he ever gets to use his escape.
If no lane fits, the camps are the better deal: you stay level with their jungler and the right lane usually appears a wave or two later.
check: Where each wave is, which enemy laner has used Flash, and whether your laner is healthy enough to follow up.
breaks: If their jungler was just seen next to that lane, it becomes a two-on-two you may lose; gank the opposite side or farm instead.

when: before 3:30
asks: should I gank at level three
three camp gank or full clear
do I gank early or keep clearing
early gank worth it
say: Cut the clear at three camps and gank the lane whose enemy is pushed up, or finish all six if nobody's overextended.
more: An early gank catches laners before they have wards down, so it often takes Flash at least.
The price is the three camps you skipped. Decide before you go whether you return to them or whether their jungler gets to walk in.
A Flash taken now is a kill window for the next few minutes, so plan the second visit on your way back through.
check: Whether a lane is actually past the middle, and which side their jungler started on.
breaks: If both side lanes are sitting near their own towers, the gank just delays your clear; finish all six camps and reach the river at about level 4.
basis: pro:An early gank is paid for in camps

when: before 4:00
asks: should I gank or full clear
do I need to gank early
my team wants ganks but I want to farm
is it okay to just farm
say: Full clear first; your champion needs levels. Gank only if a lane on your path is already winning, otherwise take crab and reset.
more: One full clear is about level 4, and a scaling jungler at level 4 brings far more to a lane than one who left at level 3 with half his camps still up.
A lane that is already winning its trade needs very little from you, so that gank is cheap. A losing lane needs a lot, and you can't supply it yet.
Being a camp ahead every clear adds up to a level lead around the first objectives.
check: Which lane your clear ends beside, and whether that lane's enemy is low or past the middle.
breaks: If their jungler is a strong early ganker and your lanes are dying, pure farming loses the map; cover the lane he is likely to visit instead.

asks: my camps are all down what now
nothing to farm should I gank
jungle's empty where do I go
camps aren't up yet
say: With your camps down a gank costs nothing, so go to the nearest lane you can reach, or recall and buy if no target's reachable.
more: Small camps take a couple of minutes to come back, so this is the cheapest moment you get to leave the jungle.
Even a gank that only forces a recall is profit here, because you gave up nothing to make it.
If you recall instead, time it so you walk back onto the first camp as it returns.
check: That your camps really are all down, how much gold you hold, and which lane has its wave on your side.
breaks: If a camp is seconds from respawning beside you, take it first; and if the only lane nearby is shoved to their tower, the recall is better.
basis: pro:Gank when your camps are down

when: an enemy laner's summoner spells do not include Flash
asks: who's the easiest gank
anyone without flash
which lane can't get away
who should I keep ganking
say: That laner took no Flash at all, so he's your repeat target all game, or pick another lane while he's hugging tower.
more: Most failed ganks fail to Flash. A laner who never had it has to play every wave as if it were already used.
Even without a kill, showing there makes him give up minions, which is a lead for your laner.
Check what he took instead: Ghost lets him outrun a slow gank, so bring crowd control.
check: Whether his champion has a dash or other escape of its own, and where the wave is.
breaks: If his champion has a built-in escape or he never leaves his tower, the missing Flash matters less; treat him like any other lane.

asks: he just flashed do I go back
flash is down top should I gank again
their mid has no flash
we burned his flash now what
say: Come back after a camp or two while his Flash is still down, or stay on your clear if the wave's now at his tower.
more: A burned Flash is the best reason there is to gank the same lane twice. The first visit was the investment and the second is the payoff.
Tell your laner you are coming so the wave is held on your side when you arrive.
He knows it too, so expect him to ward and play back; a different entrance than last time helps.
check: That Flash was really used and roughly when, and whether the wave has come back toward your side.
breaks: If several minutes have passed, assume it is back up; and if he is pinned at his tower with a ward down, go elsewhere.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: your laner is a level above their lane opponent
asks: my top is ahead should I gank him
do I gank the winning lane
gank for the lane that's up a level
say: Gank that lane while your laner holds the level lead, since he already wins the trade; or wait a wave if it's pushed to their tower.
more: A level is stats and sometimes an ability rank, so your laner can start the fight himself and you only have to finish it.
Winning lanes turn kills into plates and tower gold fastest, and a fed laner draws their jungler, which frees the other side for you.
check: Where that wave is and whether the enemy laner has backed off to his tower already.
breaks: If the enemy is freezing at his tower you'd be diving; ask your laner to let the wave come back, or dive only with a big wave.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

when: an allied laner has two or more deaths and trails their opponent in CS
asks: my top is feeding should I help
do I gank the losing lane
bot's getting destroyed do I go
should I save my laner
say: Skip that lane unless he's low and past the middle, since it risks a double kill; or gank where your laner can follow up.
more: A laner who is behind can't add much damage, so the gank is really you alone against a fed champion, with his jungler likely nearby.
What helps that lane more is clearing the camps near it and warding, so your laner can farm under tower without being dived.
Put your time where a kill becomes a tower; that lead is what covers for the lost lane later.
check: Whether the fed enemy is overextended with no ward and low enough to kill, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If he is pushed past the middle, low, and his Flash was used, it's a free shutdown; take it.
basis: pro:The jungle beside a losing lane is theirs

when: an allied laner died in the last 30 seconds
asks: my laner just died should I go there
top died do I cover the lane
bot just got killed what do I do
say: If the killer stayed to push while hurt, catch him now; or hold the wave at your tower so your laner loses less.
more: The winner of a lane fight often stays to push with little health and his abilities spent. If that's what you see, he's as gankable as he gets.
If he recalls instead, catching the wave under tower saves your laner minions and experience, which is still worth the walk.
check: How much health the killer has left, whether he used his summoner spells in the fight, and whether their jungler was part of the kill.
breaks: If their jungler was in that kill, they are two there and you are one; stay away and take camps or the far side instead.

when: their jungler got a kill or assist in the last 20 seconds
asks: their jungler just showed where do I go
he's top so do I gank bot
enemy jungle is bot side now what
say: He just showed, so the opposite side has no counter-gank for a moment; gank there now, or take his camps on that side.
more: A confirmed sighting is the only time you know a gank is truly two-on-one, and it expires as fast as he can walk back.
If the lane on your side isn't gankable, his far-side camps are free, and he comes back to an empty jungle.
check: Which lane the kill happened in, and whether he looked healthy enough to keep moving.
breaks: If the kill was in mid he can reach either side quickly; treat it as a short window and don't start a long play.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: their jungler is dead
asks: their jungler's dead what do I do
enemy jungle just died should I gank
he's dead where do I go
say: Their jungler's dead, so any gank is a real numbers edge; hit the nearest lane, or take the objective if one's up.
more: With him dead there is no counter-gank and no enemy Smite, so both a gank and an objective are safe for the length of his timer.
An objective is usually the bigger prize. Choose the gank when nothing is up or when a kill opens a tower.
check: How long is left on his respawn timer and whether a dragon, grubs or herald is actually up.
breaks: If his timer is nearly over, don't start anything long; a quick camp of his is the safe choice.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: their jungler is at least a level above you
asks: their jungler's ahead of me where do I gank
I'm behind in jungle should I still gank
he's higher level than me
say: Avoid lanes he could join, since you lose that two-on-two; gank where he just left, or farm back to even first.
more: When both junglers arrive at the same lane, the level gap decides it, and you'd be handing over a double kill.
A trailing jungler is predictable, so vary it: gank right after he shows on the other side.
Catching up on camps is not passive. A couple of clean clears is the usual way a level gap closes.
check: Where he was last seen, and which of your lanes is strong enough to carry the fight for you.
breaks: If your laner is far ahead of theirs, that lane can win the two-on-two for you, and ganking it is fine.
basis: pro:A jungler who is behind has few places to go

when: you are a level or more above their jungler
asks: I'm ahead of their jungler what do I do
should I gank or invade when ahead
I'm up a level on him
say: You're favored in the two-on-two, so gank the lane he's likely to visit and force it; or invade his camps if lanes are quiet.
more: Your lead is worth most in fights where he shows up, because he can't match you and his laner loses the wave too.
A level lead that only farms gets farmed back. Spend it on a lane or his jungle in the next couple of minutes.
check: Which side he is likely on, and whether the nearest laners on your side can move first.
breaks: If your nearby lanes are pushed in and can't follow, an invade turns against you; gank instead of going into his jungle.
basis: pro:An invade ends when the nearest lane arrives

when: their jungler is a strong early ganking champion
asks: should I counter gank
where's he going to gank
do I sit in a lane and wait for him
how do I stop their jungler ganking
say: Sit behind your most pushed-up lane briefly to catch his gank, or go back to camps if he hasn't shown by the next wave.
more: A counter-gank is the best gank there is: he has committed his abilities and your laner is already fighting.
The cost is time. Seconds spent hovering come out of your camps, so set the limit before you start waiting.
check: Which of your lanes is past the middle with no ward, and which side he started his clear on.
breaks: If you guess wrong twice you fall behind in farm; when unsure, just warn the lane and keep clearing.
basis: pro:Hovering a play that never starts costs the next clear

asks: they're ganking top should I go
he's ganking my bot lane do I help
should I counter gank that
my laner's getting ganked
say: Go only if you'll arrive while your laner's still alive and healthy; otherwise gank the far side or take his camps.
more: Arriving late to a lost fight gives them a second kill. Arriving during it flips the numbers back.
If you can't make it, you know exactly where he is, so anything on the other half of the map is free for a short while.
check: How far you are, your laner's health, and how many enemies are there.
breaks: If your laner is under his tower with Flash up, he may survive alone; a trade on the other side then pays more than the walk.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

asks: how do I come into lane
river gank or lane gank
where do I gank from
they keep seeing me coming
say: Come through the lane brush or around behind him if river's likely warded; otherwise walk in from river, since it's faster.
more: A lane gank takes longer but comes from where laners rarely ward, so the target reacts later.
Coming around behind him cuts off the walk home, but it only works while he's far from his tower, and it leaves you deep if their jungler turns up.
check: Whether you saw a ward placed in river or the side brush, and where the wave sits.
breaks: If the wave is already under your tower, a slow loop wastes the window; walk straight in from river.

when: before 3:30 and the bot laners are level 1 or 2
asks: should I gank bot early
bot lane is fighting at level one do I go
two camp gank bot

say: If the enemy duo fought hard and kept pushing, a two-camp clear into bot punishes it, or full clear if they've backed off.
more: A lane that trades summoner spells at level one and keeps pushing has a long way home and nothing left to escape with.
You give up most of your first clear for it, so it needs to be a kill or two Flashes, not a maybe.
check: Whether summoner spells were used, whether they are past the middle, and whether a ward went down in the brush or river.
breaks: If your own bot lane is the one that lost the trade and is low, they can't follow up; full clear and come later.
basis: pro:A lane that fights early without a ward invites a short clear

asks: should I gank mid
is mid gankable
mid or side lane
why do my mid ganks fail
say: Mid's a short lane, so gank it only with crowd control or a burned Flash; otherwise pick a side lane with more room.
more: In mid the tower is always close, so you get one ability on him before he's safe. It has to be a stun or he has to be Flashless.
A mid gank that works pays the most though: your mid can then move first to both rivers for the next objective.
check: Whether your mid has crowd control ready, and whether their mid's Flash or dash was used.
breaks: If their mid is pushed to your tower and low, even a no-crowd-control gank works; go.

asks: top side or bot side
which side should I play
gank top or bot
where should I path
say: Gank the side where the next objective spawns, so a kill becomes that objective; or the other side if only that lane's gankable.
more: A kill next to a live objective pays twice. A kill on the far side often pays once, and they take the objective meanwhile.
Path so you finish your camps on that side about half a minute before the spawn.
check: Which objective is next, and which of those lanes actually has its wave on your side.
breaks: If the lane beside the objective is shoved to their tower, forcing it fails; gank the other side and trade objectives.

when: between 6:30 and 8:00
asks: should I gank before grubs
grubs are coming where do I go
how do I set up grubs
top or bot before eight minutes
say: Gank top or mid before 8:00 so grubs start with a numbers edge, or path bot for dragon if top's stuck under tower.
more: Grubs are one window and do not come back, so a kill or forced recall top just before 8:00 often decides all of them.
If your top side can't move, don't force it. Trading for a dragon on the other side is a fair result.
check: Whether your top and mid can leave their waves, and where their jungler is pathing.
breaks: If their top laner has Teleport and yours does not, a forced recall buys less; count who arrives before committing.

when: a dragon is up or spawns within a minute
asks: dragon's up should I gank bot
gank or just take dragon
how do I get dragon
bot or mid before dragon
say: Gank bot or mid now, because a kill or forced recall there turns straight into dragon; or start it if their jungler showed top.
more: Dragon is decided by who can walk to it. Removing one bot or mid laner for half a minute is usually enough.
If the gank fails, you are still on the right side of the map with your lanes nearby.
check: Whether bot and mid waves are pushed, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If the gank leaves you low before the spawn, it cost you the dragon; skip it when your health is poor and just set up.
basis: pro:A low or dead enemy mid makes the river yours

asks: gank failed what now
he got away what do I do
that gank didn't work
wasted a gank now what
say: Leave straight away and take the nearest camp so the trip costs seconds, or help shove the wave if your laner needs a recall.
more: The gank is over when he reaches his tower. Standing in lane after that shares your laner's experience and shows their jungler where you are.
Note what was used. A burned Flash or ultimate makes the next visit much better.
check: Which camp is closest and up, and whether your laner wants the wave pushed.
breaks: If he is still low and the wave is arriving at his tower, that's a dive setup rather than a failed gank; check the dive conditions.
basis: pro:Hovering a play that never starts costs the next clear

asks: I've ganked top twice and nothing
should I keep ganking the same lane
he keeps getting away
third gank top?
say: Stop going there unless the last try burned his Flash; he's safe near tower. Put that time into another lane or your camps.
more: A good reason to gank does not make it work on a champion who is safe near his tower.
Each failed trip costs a camp or two, and after two of them their jungler is simply ahead of you.
The lane can still be helped by a ward and by clearing the camps beside it.
check: Whether the last gank forced Flash or an ultimate, and where the wave is now.
breaks: If Flash did go down and the wave is back on your side, one more visit soon is justified.
basis: pro:Stop repeating a gank that keeps failing

when: you died in the last 30 seconds
asks: I died ganking what now
I inted that gank
how do I recover from a bad gank
I just died in lane
say: Don't force another gank to win it back. Clear from whichever side respawned, or cover the lane he'll likely visit next.
more: A death costs you camps and gives him a free play. A second forced gank usually doubles the loss.
Farming is what puts you back level, and clean clears repair an early death better than a forced play.
check: Which of your camps are up, and where their jungler went after the kill.
breaks: If their jungler also died or is very low, the map is even again and a normal gank is fine.

when: you got a kill or assist in the last 30 seconds and hold enough gold for an item component

should I back after the gank

more: Gold in your pocket does nothing. The jungler who bought picks the next fight while the other is still on old items.
Help shove the wave before you recall so your laner can go too and the enemy loses the minions.
check: How much gold you hold and what it buys, and whether a camp is about to return.
breaks: If an objective is spawning within seconds and you are healthy, stay for it and buy afterwards.
basis: pro:Skipping the recall keeps camp pace but not power

when: you got a kill or assist in a lane in the last 20 seconds

say: Help push the wave into his tower so he loses minions, then leave; or stay for plates only if their jungler showed elsewhere.
more: A kill is paid out by the wave. If it crashes into his tower while he's dead, he loses gold and experience on top of the death.
Don't stay long. You are visible, and their jungler now knows which half of the map is free.
check: How big the wave is, the enemy laner's respawn timer, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If you are low and their jungler is unseen, leave at once; a traded kill undoes most of the gank.

should I keep ganking bot
play around one lane?

more: Camping works when each kill makes the next one easier: a snowballing champion against an immobile one.
The cost is the other half of the map. Expect their jungler to take camps and pressure the far lane.
Plan your clears to end beside that lane, so camping it costs as little farm as possible.
check: Whether that enemy has a dash or Flash, and whether your laner's champion uses a lead well.
breaks: If the far-side laner is being dived repeatedly, the trade has turned; go back to covering both sides.

when: your bot lane has an engage support such as Leona, Nautilus, Alistar or Thresh

is bot gankable

bot or top

more: With a hook or a stun from the support, you don't need to land anything first. You only need to be close when it connects.
A bot kill is often two kills and sits next to dragon.
check: Whether your support is healthy and has the engage ability ready, and where the bot wave is.
breaks: If the enemy support has a way to stop crowd control, such as Morgana's Black Shield, wait for it to be used first.

when: the enemy laner has a dash or blink, such as Ezreal, Tristana or Ahri at level 6

how do I gank someone with a dash
say: That gank's usually wasted because he jumps away; go once you've seen the escape used, or pick the lane with an immobile target.

check: Whether his escape ability was just used, and whether your laner can lock him down.

which enemy do I focus early
easiest kill on their team

Two visits a few minutes apart is the usual pattern, so plan your clear to pass that lane again.
check: Whether he has Flash up and where his wave is.
breaks: If his support or lane partner has strong peel, the gank needs to be fast; choose the solo lane instead.

asks: my laner is pushing can I gank
wave is at their tower should I come
top keeps shoving and pinging me
can I gank a pushed lane

more: A gank needs space between the target and his tower. A shoved wave removes all of it.
The pushed lane does give you something else: your laner can move first, so river and their camps on that side are safer.
check: Where the wave is and whether your laner can actually stop pushing.
breaks: If he is low under tower with a big wave arriving, a dive can work; check his defensive ability and their jungler first.

asks: is this gank worth it
am I wasting time ganking
should I gank or farm
when is a gank a waste

more: Every gank is priced in camps. A walk across the map for a maybe is how junglers fall a level behind.
Ganks that are on the way between two camps cost almost nothing, so path to make them cheap.
check: Which camps are up, how far the lane is, and where the wave sits.
breaks: If the target is low with no Flash, the price is worth paying even with camps up.

check: Which laners are still level 5 and whether your laner has his ultimate too.
breaks: If their jungler is also 6 and nearby, the edge is gone; pick the lane on the far side from him.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

almost six do I gank
do I farm to six first

check: How close you are to 6, and whether a camp or crab is alive near the lane.
breaks: If the camp is a long way from the lane, go now; the detour costs more than the level gives.
basis: pro:A crab can be the level that wins the skirmish

when: the enemy laner is level 6 and your laner in that lane is level 5

is it safe to gank a level six

One more wave usually fixes it, so clear a nearby camp and come back.
check: How close your laner is to 6 and whether the enemy ultimate was just used.
breaks: If their ultimate was just spent, the gap is only stats; go now.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

asks: bot or a solo lane

two kills bot or one top
why gank bot

When they work they pay more: possibly two kills, and dragon is next to it.

asks: who do I gank in mid game

check: Who is showing in side lanes, how many enemies are missing, and the next objective timer.

basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

asks: my laner is pinging me to gank

do I drop my camp to gank
should I listen to the gank ping

A ping tells you the laner wants help, not that the lane is gankable. Judge the wave yourself.
check: Where that wave is, the enemy's health, and how long the walk is.
breaks: If the enemy is very low and already in a fight with your laner, leave the camp and go.

when: an enemy laner is a late-game scaling champion such as Kayle, Nasus or Kassadin

do I camp the nasus
who do I stop from scaling

Even without kills, your presence lets your laner deny him the wave.
check: Whether he is pushed out far enough to reach, and whether your laner can hold him.
breaks: If he never leaves tower range, take the objectives his weak lane can't contest instead.

when: your health is below half

more: A low jungler turns a gank into a target for the enemy laner, and for their jungler if he's near.
